_README: REAL PUBLISHED SUSPENDED-SEDIMENT FIGURES, for sanity-checking this tool's
own assumptions against the real world - not for calibrating the baseline
model directly (data/trials.json's real bench trials do that; see
lib/baseline.ts). This is the plan's rebuild phase 8, 'validation loop':
named-river context, not a new calibration input.
Every figure here was found via a live web search this session (not
recalled from training data). `confidence` is a plain low/medium/high/
insufficient-data rating; `confidenceReason` says exactly why - several
of these are secondary citations or search-engine-summarised snippets,
not numbers read directly from the original paper's own tables. Where a
search could not pin down a solid, specific figure (the River Dee), that
is recorded honestly as confidence: insufficient-data, suspendedSedimentMgL
null - a real gap, not a placeholder number standing in for one. Same
rule this project applies everywhere else: insufficient data is not a
negative outcome, it is the honest outcome.
`comparisonNote` on each entry is this project's own read on how the
figure relates to lib/baseline.ts's calibration reference (3274 mg/L,
the mean of this project's own 10 real bench trials).

studies.location: Tidal Thames, Mud Reaches (estuary, not the freshwater river)
studies.citation: Baugh, J. & Littlewood, M. (2005), three-layer model of fine-sediment transport in the Thames estuary
studies.foundVia: Cited in a supplementary document for a 2015 HESSD preprint - the original paper itself was not read directly this session
studies.confidenceReason: Secondary citation, model output not a field measurement, original paper not read directly.
studies.note: Tidal- and width-averaged turbidity maximum: ~150 mg/L at neap tides, ~600 mg/L at spring tides, in the Mud Reaches.
studies.comparisonNote: Even at the spring-tide high end (600 mg/L), this sits well below this tool's 3274 mg/L calibration reference - see the file-level finding in BUILD.md.

studies.citation: HR Wallingford report summarising Thames field surveys, 1969-1983
studies.foundVia: Web search snippet of the report's own summary table
studies.measurementKind: field survey (reported in ppm, taken as approximately equal to mg/L for dilute suspensions)
studies.confidenceReason: The source document's own OCR text is poor quality per the search tool's own assessment; spans spring AND neap tides pooled together, not directly comparable across surveys.
studies.note: August 1969 Woolwich survey: 300-2630 ppm. October 1981 survey, various sites: 97-4720 ppm. Real field data, but a wide, tide-state-mixed range, not a single representative figure.
studies.comparisonNote: The upper end of this real field range (4720 mg/L) does exceed this tool's 3274 mg/L reference - tidal Thames during a strong flood tide can be more concentrated than this tool assumes, though the low end is far below it.

studies.foundVia: Multiple web searches this session, none surfacing a specific, citable mg/L figure
studies.confidenceReason: No specific mg/L figure was found, not a placeholder or a guess.
studies.note: Real studies exist (Amoudry et al. 2014, Ocean Dynamics, DOI 10.1007/s10236-014-0695-8; Bolanos, Moate & Souza 2009; a 2025 planning-inspectorate chapter citing Hilbre Channel data) but none of their concentration VALUES appeared in what a web search could surface this session - only that concentration is tide-controlled, which is already known. Reading the original papers directly would be the next step, not something this session could do.

studies.location: The Narrows (estuary, between Liverpool and Birkenhead)
studies.citation: Prandle et al. (1990), cited via Coastal Wiki
studies.foundVia: Web search summary of a secondary source (Coastal Wiki), not the original 1990 paper
studies.confidenceReason: Specific, attributed figures, but read from a secondary citation rather than the original paper.
studies.note: Cross-sectional mean SPM of ~32 mg/L at a tidal amplitude of 2.6 m, rising to ~213 mg/L at 4.0 m - concentration scales strongly with tidal range.
studies.comparisonNote: Well below this tool's 3274 mg/L reference across the whole reported range - the Mersey Narrows under normal tidal conditions is far less concentrated than this tool's bench-trial calibration assumes.

studies.location: ~1700 km of the Lower Mekong River, from river to estuary
studies.citation: Le, T.B. et al. (2020), 'Suspended sediment properties in the Lower Mekong River, from fluvial to estuarine environments', Estuarine, Coastal and Shelf Science, 233, 106522
studies.foundVia: Web search of the paper's own abstract and accepted-manuscript snippets
studies.measurementKind: laboratory flocculation-behaviour testing across a concentration range, not a single ambient field reading
studies.confidenceReason: The paper's own abstract states a much wider lab-test range (20-30,000 mg/L) than the accepted manuscript (400-4000 mg/L); the 400 mg/L flocculation threshold itself was consistent across every source checked, so that specific figure is the reliable part.
studies.note: Identifies a real flocculation threshold at ~400 mg/L: above this, flocculation and sedimentation increase by orders of magnitude, and fluid mud layers may form. 75% of suspended sediment by volume is flocculated aggregates, not discrete grains - a real caveat for this tool's own hydrocyclone math, which assumes discrete-particle density separation.
studies.comparisonNote: This tool's 3274 mg/L reference sits comfortably inside the Mekong's real flocculation-prone range - unlike the UK rivers above, a Mekong-like feed at this tool's assumed concentration would likely already be flocculating, which changes separation behaviour in ways this tool does not model (see data/screening-parameters.json's flocDensityPenalty note).

studies.citation: Beveridge, Hossain & Bonnema, satellite-based 31-year suspended-sediment record of the 3S tributaries
studies.measurementKind: satellite-derived estimate of CHANGE in concentration (not an absolute level) attributed to dam construction (+120 mg/L near a basin outlet) and reservoir trapping (-108 mg/L)
studies.confidenceReason: A specific, attributed figure with a stated RMSE (21.2 mg/L), but a satellite-derived estimate, not direct sampling.
studies.note: A different kind of figure from the others here: how much dam construction and operation SHIFT concentration, not an absolute ambient level. Relevant context for how much a catchment's real sediment regime can move over decades, not directly comparable to a single calibration reference.
